topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of the lecture, outlining how known immune molecules and cells combine to initiate and resolve inflammation.

topics.label: Innate pathogen and damage recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects infections and tissue injury through pattern recognition receptors and their intracellular signaling mechanisms.

topics.label: Inflammatory response mechanisms and systemic consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated innate cells coordinate leukocyte recruitment, lymphatic priming, and systemic pathology during an acute inflammatory response.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the immune system terminates inflammation to enable tissue repair and how persistent stimuli lead to chronic adaptations such as granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the topic of the subsequent lecture.
